reason: The first reading was reread on the images with the Ordinal and the Vulgate at hand, which resolved the rubric 'In laudibus antiphone', the interleaved verse 'convenerant' with its cue 'Petrus', and the order of the four pages.
sources: S. J. P. van Dijk and J. Hazelden Walker, The Ordinal of the Papal Court from Innocent III to Boniface VIII (Fribourg 1975), pp. 243-244, 259-260 (Google Books snippets)
'S. François et la liturgie', Archivum Franciscanum Historicum 19 (1926), p. 92 (archive.org text)

SOURCE-ASSISTED READING (stams-2026-10-30b), made with the Ordinal of the papal court (Van Dijk and Walker 1975, snippets) and the Vulgate at hand. Reread on the native images by a research reader: canvas 0 columns 1 and 2 complete and the top half of column 3; canvas 1 column 2 lower half, column 3 complete, column 4 lower half. Canvas 1 column 1 (Lam 4:4-14) was read on the image by an independent research reader. All other lines rest on the image-only first reading. Expansions in ( ); [ ] lost, damaged or supplied; (?) uncertain; | line break. Neumes not transcribed.

Images: https://fragmentarium.ms/loris/F-5z6w/Stams_STA_Frg_113_01r.jpg (canvas 0) and https://fragmentarium.ms/loris/F-5z6w/Stams_STA_Frg_113_01v.jpg (canvas 1), each 7360 x 4912. Regions x,y,width,height in native pixels. Columns numbered 1-4 from the left of each face. Text order: canvas 1 cols 3-4, canvas 0 cols 1-4, canvas 1 cols 1-2.
